source_document.source_file: Singlife/Medical & Life Insurance/Maternity Insurance/Singlife Maternity Care.md

extraction.document_summary: Singlife Maternity Care is a Singapore Life (Singlife) single-premium, 3-year maternity plan designed to cover the mother and the child for expenses/financial assistance arising from pregnancy complications and newborn-related conditions. For the mother, it provides coverage for “Death” and specified “Pregnancy complications,” each with a cover limit of 100% of sum assured, plus “Hospital care” with a cover limit of 1% of sum assured for each day of hospitalisation, capped at up to 30 days (subject to a separate rule that the hospital care benefit ends when 30% of the sum assured is paid or when the contract term ends—whichever is earlier). For the child, it similarly covers death, congenital illnesses, and hospital care (1% per day up to 30 days), and adds coverage for severe neonatal jaundice outpatient phototherapy (1% per day up to 30 days), stem cell transplant surgery (50% of sum assured), and developmental delay (10% of sum assured). It is purchasable within the application pregnancy window (13 to 36 weeks) and subject to eligibility ages (18 to 45 ANB).
quality_notes: Benefit schedule includes many listed conditions but the payout limit row is partially formatted, requiring reliance on the clearly stated Important Notes for stem cell transplant (50% of sum assured) and developmental delay (10% of sum assured).
Some limit text for child benefits (e.g., stem cell treatment row) appears inconsistently formatted, so numeric parsing is supplemented by the Important Notes section.
Underwriting method/medical screening for the maternity plan itself is not stated; only the option to buy a new whole life plan for the child without medical underwriting is described.

policies.quick_summary: A single-premium 3-year maternity plan covering the mother and child for pregnancy complications, congenital illnesses, and hospitalisation-related expenses, with additional child benefits for outpatient phototherapy (severe neonatal jaundice), stem cell transplant surgery, and developmental delay. Mother/child “Death” and “Pregnancy complications/ Congenital illnesses” are covered at 100% of sum assured, while hospital/phototherapy care is covered at 1% of sum assured per day up to 30 days, subject to a hospital-care end rule for the mother (30% of sum assured paid or contract term ends). Child stem cell transplant pays 50% of sum assured; developmental delay pays 10% of sum assured.
coverage_scope: Mother: death, pregnancy complications, hospital care
Child(ren): death, congenital illnesses, hospital care
Child(ren): outpatient phototherapy for severe neonatal jaundice
Child(ren): stem cell transplant surgery (for transplant surgery only)
policies.eligibility_notes: Applicant must be between 18 and 45 years old (both ages inclusive) and within 13 to 36 weeks (both weeks inclusive) of pregnancy at the time of application.
policy_termination_events: Hospital care benefit ends when 30% of the sum assured is paid or when the contract term ends—whichever is earlier
Hospital care benefit ends when 30% of the sum assured is paid or when the contract term ends—whichever is earlier (as stated for the Hospital care benefits(s) for the Mother (or child))
important_caveats: As stated: “This refers to the Hospital care benefits(s) for the Mother (or child). The Hospital care benefit(s) will end when 30% of the sum assured is paid or when the contract term ends – whichever is earlier.”
Child stem cell transplant and developmental delay benefits end when the stated percentage of sum assured is paid or when the contract term ends—whichever is earlier.
The brochure states the policy has “no savings or investment feature”, and therefore there is no cash value if the policy ends or ends prematurely.

A separate option exists within 90 days from the birth of an insured child to buy a new whole life plan for the insured child without medical underwriting, subject to stated maximum total death/TI/TPD benefit amounts and a “pre-existing conditions” restriction.

review_notes: No separately marketed base plan tiers/options were explicitly identified in the brochure; only a worked illustration and a single example coverage amount (S$10,000) were provided.

Outpatient phototherapy payout limit row formatting is inconsistent; benefit is extracted using the schedule line and the “severe neonatal jaundice” trigger, but the numeric basis is recorded with low confidence.
